title: Tying Component Assembly/Wiring directly with Runtime Configurations
damaged_code:
```yaml
# Spring/wiring configuration mixing object associations with credentials
beans:
  - id: databaseConnection
    class: com.system.infra.DbConnection
    properties:
      - host: "10.0.0.12"
      - password: "production_clear_password" # Sensitive environmental secret
  - id: billingService
    class: com.system.domain.BillingService
    properties:
      - database: { ref: databaseConnection } # Code assembly / wiring
```
pattern: A single configuration file contains both sensitive runtime parameters (passwords, IP addresses, tokens) and basic application code assembly/wiring rules (object instantiation, bean references).
why_bad: Forces operators or administrators to edit highly volatile, complex structure files just to update a simple password. A single typo in the 5,000-line XML/YAML code-assembly section of the file can break core object references, causing obscure runtime crashes.
detection: Configuration files where database/service credentials and connection variables are combined with classpath, object hierarchy, or reference mappings.
counterexample: Simple metadata manifest descriptors. Marked as `Strong`.
fix:
Keep application object wiring entirely separate from sensitive runtime configurations. Sensitive properties should be loaded in separate files or environment variables, or injected as external properties.
```yaml
# separate file: credentials.env
DB_PASSWORD="production_clear_password"
```
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!* (2007), Chapter 14.2, "Configuration Files", p. 598-599.
